customer-acme: Hi — since ~08:30 UTC our API calls that used to hit eu-west-1 are seeing 300-800ms additional latency and traces show hops to us-west-2. No config change on our side. Can you help?

maria_support: Thanks — sorry about that. Do you have a sample request-id and region header we can look up?

customer-acme: req=4b2f9c0a, host=api.redwood.example, we set region=eu-west in SDK config.

maria_support: Got it. Opening an investigation. Ingesting traces now (req 4b2f9c0a).ingest-bot: New support ticket created #S-12345 for req=4b2f9c0a.

ben_sre: I see the trace — client DNS resolved to eu VIP but downstream envoy shows route to us-west-2 pool. Possible fallback. Any recent route_preference changes?

ryan_netops: We rolled a change last night that tightened capacity thresholds for eu pool and added an emergency fallback to the global pool. That should only activate at 99.99p, but might be noisy on the short tail.

maria_support: Can you confirm whether the fallback path respects SNI/host header? If SNI mismatch the global LB might send to us-west.

ben_sre: Good question. Looking at load-balancer logs for that trace id: host header preserved, SNI identical. But the chosen backend was from global pool due to this health-check flapping: backend eu-32 returned 503 on two consecutive warmup checks at 08:29:57.

customer-acme: We saw some 5xx around that time but assumed transient. Is that why we're routed across region? That's surprising for short requests.

ryan_netops: Yes — fallback is sticky per connection and can create cross-region hops for a small percent of requests during backend churn. We should have TTL-based stickiness, but appears we used session affinity without locality.

ben_sre: Quick mitigation: I pushed a rollback to the fallback selector to prefer same-region backends unless capacity is completely exhausted. Rolling back should finish in ~2 min. Can you pls re-run a few requests and share traces?

maria_support: Also ask customer to run traceroute to the VIP and capture DNS TTL: `dig +short api.redwood.example` and `dig +trace api.redwood.example` — want to confirm resolver behavior and EDNS-client-subnet.

customer-acme: Running now. dig shows A=34.89.120.11 (eu VIP) TTL=58. traceroute shows hop to cloud-eu-edge then straight to us-west-2 after the LB. I'll upload trace and curl verbose.

ben_sre: Thanks — that confirms DNS correct; LB is deciding to forward to us-west. Rollback complete, can you re-check?

customer-acme: New trace (req=9f1a3e2b) looks much better, p50 latency back to normal. Still seeing ~0.5% of requests with an extra 200ms — probably leftover sticky sessions.

ryan_netops: We'll invalidate those session affinities and purge LB stick table entries for that VIP. ETA ~10min. Also will add a safeguard so the fallback selector prefers same-region instances by default.

maria_support: Summary for the ticket: transient eu backend health-check flapping triggered emergency global fallback; fallback selector allowed cross-region routing; rollback and affinity purge started; follow-ups: add locality preference to fallback selector and improve health-check smoothing.

customer-acme: Thanks team — appreciate the fast follow-up. Please keep us posted on the postmortem. :pray:

ingest-bot: Ticket #S-12345 updated: status -> investigating -> mitigated
